static_traits.name: Chen Bei
static_traits.social_status: A few friends and acquaintances worry about their mental health; keeping in touch with a few close friends but not yet proactively confiding Self-doubt
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; has not received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperation, able to self-Reflect; tone revealing Anxiety and Self-denial tendencies; able to describe trigger situations and impacts concretely

basic_info.main_problem: Due to works being hard to monetize years ago, gradually developing Self-doubt and incompetence feelings related to film creation; especially prominent When thinking about career and financial stability, affecting motivation and enjoyment of creation, often labeling oneself with 'I am not creative enough/not good enough'.
basic_info.core_demands: 'These self-doubts affect my motivation and enjoyment in film creation; film creation used to bring me happiness.' Hoping to reduce self-doubt, restore motivation and enjoyment for film creation, and establish a more balanced, realistic self-evaluation.
growth_experiences: A few years ago struggling to monetize film creation, beginning to continuously question own creativity and ability. Whenever thinking of Career development and financial stability, feeling pressure and unease; this experience became the starting point of Self-doubt and continuously Reinforced negative self-labels.

Having won multiple film festival awards and received positive audience feedback in the past, but the client tends to ignore this positive evidence, focusing more on self-perceived failures and financial unsuccess, so positive experiences cannot yet convert into stable Self-efficacy.

A recent short film was selected by a famous film festival and screened; at that time they felt proud and excited, briefly acknowledging their own ability and seeing career possibilities; this event provided a positive contrast to their inherent negative narrative.

special_situations.event: When works cannot yet monetize or income is unstable
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my films cannot make money, it means I am not talented enough, not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proving own capability by constantly investing in more projects, doubling Work
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I never earn money, which shows I am not creative enough

special_situations.event: When thinking about Career development and financial stability
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot make a living from what I love, I count as a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focusing all attention on Work and output, trying to Undoing unease with effort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot do it, I may never be able to gain a foothold in this industry

special_situations.event: When comparing with more successful filmmakers
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach their achievements, I am utterly worthless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent self-criticism, evaluating oneself with negative labels
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them, will never reach their level

special_situations.event: When facing the opportunity to open up to supportive friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I expose Self-doubt, others will see me as a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding sharing, keeping emotions bottled up, not asking others for help
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will look down on me, treat me as a failure

special_situations.event: When receiving awards or positive feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only financial success counts as real success, other recognition does not matter
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating or downplaying positive evidence, continuing to use profitability as the only self-evaluation standard
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These do not count, real success is making money

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as creative and valuable, hopes to be seen and affirmed in the film industry and to gain a sense of stability
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as a failure, fearing rejection and devaluation, worrying about losing self-worth from being unable to make a living from film
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being judged by over-investing in work to prove themselves, avoiding exposing vulnerability to friends, and maintaining a controllable evaluation standard through self-labeling

object_relations.object_representation: Others who are more excellent and may judge oneself (successful filmmakers / others)

object_relations.self_representation: Vulnerable person worried about being seen as a failure
object_relations.object_representation: Friends who are supportive but may see oneself as a failure (imagined judges)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores sharing Self-doubt with friends or encourages focusing on and recording positive achievements
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to think others will see her as a failure (transference: projecting her own sense of failure onto others' possible views)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a gentle, empathic tone, first validate their worries; then invite them to adduce the facts and counterexamples of 'others seeing them as a failure', distinguish imagination from evidence; encourage balancing the self-evaluation with concrete experiences (awards/screenings), and avoid confrontational wording.

manifestations: After works are hard to profit from, questions the meaning of filmmaking and self-worth
Equates 'financial success' with 'life/career meaning', ignoring achievements and satisfaction at non-financial levels
outcomes: Decreased drive and reduced creative enjoyment
Unbalanced life; neglecting self-care and socializing

manifestations: Living alone and not yet opening up to supportive friends about Self-doubt
Worrying about being seen as a failure and emotionally self-isolating
outcomes: Reduces real contact and support obtained in important relationships

contact_model.definition: An individual restraining the impulse to do something to other people or things, or giving up seeking others to do something for them, turning to oneself instead; i.e., redirecting energy originally sent outward back toward oneself.
manifestations: Not expressing Self-doubt to supportive friends, instead pressuring oneself
Through doubling investment in projects to 'prove oneself', directing energy toward self-control rather than outside support

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treats the external standard of 'must make a living from film to count as success' as the sole criterion for evaluation
Under financial pressure, measures self-worth with profit as the core, ignores awards and audience praise

exception_events.target_problem: When thinking about career and financial stability or when works do not yet monetize, the client usually Self-denies, labels with 'no creativity', and ignores positive feedback, leading to Decreased drive and reduced enjoyment of creation.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A recent short film was selected by a prestigious film festival and screened; the client did not negate themselves as before, but felt proud and excited, and generated the thought 'maybe I am capable of gaining a foothold in the industry'.
exception_events.reason: Clue: gaining objective recognition from an authoritative platform and positive external feedback provided concrete, visible evidence of success, enabling them to temporarily break free from the old narrative of 'negating the positive' at that moment.

positive_force: Has creative ability and external recognition (won film festival awards and audience praise, work selected for a famous film festival)
Has a few close friends supporting his film passion
Willing to seek help, Positive attitude with self-Reflection ability
negative_force: Strong Self-doubt, often defining self with negative labels
Comparison with others leading to inferiority and despair
Negating positive evidence, using profitability as the only success standard
Financial pressure Reinforcing Anxiety and low self-efficacy
Emotional avoidance and not expressing distress to friends, weakening the gain of Social support

target_behavior.behavior: Over-investing in film projects to escape Self-doubt, leading to neglected self-care and social life
antecedent: Thinking about Career development and financial stability
When works do not yet monetize or income is unstable
After comparing with more successful filmmakers
target_behavior.core_reason: Binding profitability to self-worth, proving capability with 'doubling Work' in negative emotions, controlling unease
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome emotions (Self-doubt/shame/Anxiety), and trying to gain external confirmation of capability and value
target_behavior.consequence: Life imbalance and increased physical and mental load instead impair motivation and creativity, further reducing enjoyment of creating

target_behavior.behavior: Self-evaluating with negative labels (e.g., 'I have no creativity''I am not good enough')
antecedent: When thinking about career and financial stability
When the economic return of works is poor
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizing external success standards (profit/status) and negating positive evidence, generalizing temporary setbacks into stable self-defects
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a 'controllable' self-Interpretation framework through self-criticism, avoiding facing uncertainty and vulnerability
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased self-confidence, damaged motivation and creativity, further increasing avoidance and life imbalance
